import CERegistry from "/src/index.ts"; /** * The panels are loaded by the real registry — there is no stand-in here. * `catalog` maps the tag to a loader and `src/lifecycle.ts` paints the walk * itself, so what the CSS above is hooked to is the shipped state machine: * * :not(:defined) → [ce=loading] → [ce=loaded] → [ce=defined] * └─ defer barrier ─┘ * * `loaded` is the window `deferDefine` opens: the module is in memory, the * batch has not upgraded yet. `defined` is written in the frame the element * upgrades and is the last state of the success walk, which is why every * reveal above is declared on it alone. */ const PANEL = ` .inner { height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; display: grid; align-content: end; gap: .2rem; padding: 1.25rem; border-radius: inherit; color: #fff; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #6366f1, #ec4899 55%, #f59e0b); } h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; } p { margin: 0; font-size: .8rem; opacity: .85; } `; class DemoPanel extends HTMLElement { connectedCallback() { if (this.shadowRoot) return; this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" }).innerHTML = `

${this.getAttribute("label") ?? "component"}

${this.getAttribute("desc") ?? "revealed on [ce=defined]"}

`; } } /** A loader that takes its time, so `loading` is a state you can see. */ const slow = (ctor) => async () => { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 900)); return ctor; }; globalThis.registry = new CERegistry({ catalog: { "demo-panel": slow(DemoPanel) }, }); /* A defined tag cannot un-define itself, so a replay is a reload. */ document.getElementById("replay").addEventListener("click", () => location.reload());
